comments.body:
Phase 1 RCA + legitimacy/design escalation (2026-08-18).

Problem: a running rebar process can fail with ImportError/FileNotFoundError while a sibling executes `uv tool install --force`. No production code was edited.

Confirmed mechanism: uv 0.12.3 deliberately removes the existing tool virtualenv in place before recreating it at the same pathname. Official uv CLI docs for `uv tool install --force` say it “will recreate any existing environment.” Current upstream `crates/uv/src/commands/tool/install.rs:505-520` makes the existing environment unavailable under `force`; `:679-682` contains an explicit TODO to build elsewhere before removing the current install; `:1025-1030` calls environment creation. `crates/uv-tool/src/lib.rs:315-350` calls `remove_virtualenv` before `create_venv`. A running rebar invocation remains pathname-coupled after startup: packaged routing and guides are read lazily (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:269-279,660-688`), engine assets resolve from the installed tree (`src/rebar/_engine.py:23-46`), and children use the installed `sys.executable`/source path (`src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:252-283`; `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:188-223`). The repository snapshot layer snapshots the reviewed Git tree, not the executing distribution (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`).

Discriminating runtime proof: an isolated non-editable uv-tool install of this wheel plus `[agents]` ran a synchronized real child process. The no-reinstall control passed late import, packaged-resource read, engine resolution, and same-runtime child launch. Releasing only after a completed force reinstall also passed all probes even though the tool-directory inode changed, rejecting a broken replacement, stale-bytecode, resolver, and inode-change explanation. Releasing precisely when a 1 ms watcher observed the installed `rebar/__init__.py` absent reproduced 5/5: late `rebar.metrics` import -> ModuleNotFoundError; plan-registry import/resource -> ModuleNotFoundError; the real `_cli.main(["explain","plan"])` path -> ModuleNotFoundError at `rebar._logging`; `engine_dir()` -> missing-directory RuntimeError; child launch through `sys.executable` -> FileNotFoundError. Preimporting plan-registry code before deletion kept that code resident, but its next packaged `criteria_routing.json` read failed FileNotFoundError, rejecting “late Python import only” and proving independent resource lifetime exposure. Holding a POSIX shared flock on `UV_TOOL_DIR/.lock` made the real force install wait and left the environment intact, confirming the deletion window and showing one possible coordination primitive.

Defect legitimacy: upstream uv behavior is documented/intended. For rebar this is fail-closed `cannot-determine`, not yet an automatic defect repair: README.md:216-335 documents unpacked pip/pipx/uvx installs and on-disk engine resources but no promise that an arbitrary destructive reinstall is safe concurrently. The ticket’s desired lifetime rule would create a new release lifecycle/lease contract.

Caller-dependency gate: no narrow eager-import/resource-copy patch covers the class. A lifetime lock is tolerable for finite CLI gates but a public library embedding, MCP server, or review-bot process can live indefinitely; detached enrichment/compaction children outlive the parent and need lease transfer/refcounting. uv’s `.lock` is global to every tool, so holding it for a long-lived rebar process blocks unrelated uv-tool operations and couples rebar to uv private/cross-platform lock behavior. The managed host updater provides useful prior art (versioned releases + atomic `current`) but currently prunes every non-current release immediately; it has no reader/child lease.

Decision required before Phase 2. Recommended architectural contract: publish immutable versioned runtimes through an atomic selector, have every supported launcher/library/server invocation acquire a release lease transferable to spawned children, and garbage-collect an obsolete release only after its last lease exits; direct `uv tool install --force` against the active environment must be prohibited or wrapped because it cannot honor a rebar-only lease. Alternative A: acquire uv’s global shared tool lock for every process lifetime (simpler, but long-lived processes block all uv-tool updates and rely on private semantics). Alternative B: explicitly classify concurrent force reinstall as unsupported operator behavior and document/use only the managed atomic updater. Per rebar-debug, Phase 2 is stopped pending the intended lifecycle contract.

compiled_state.description:
## Client report
While one rebar gate invocation was running, a sibling agent executed `uv tool install --force`. uv garbage-collected the release directory backing the active process, and the gate later crashed with `ImportError` / `FileNotFoundError`. Expected behavior: an invocation resolves one installed release and keeps all code/resources it needs reachable for its entire lifetime, even when another process force-reinstalls the tool.

The reported explanation is a hypothesis until reproduced and traced. Investigation must distinguish uv installation semantics, Python import timing, subprocess/module resource lookup, and any rebar-controlled launcher or snapshot seam.

## Plan
- Reproduce with two synchronized real processes: pause an invocation after startup but before a late import/resource read, force-reinstall from the sibling process, then release the gate.
- Trace the exact path removed and the first late read/import that reaches it; compare against a no-reinstall control and uv upstream behavior.
- Establish the authoritative lifecycle contract and bounded caller/deployment impact before repair.
- After confirmed RCA, create a held-out parent/child subprocess RED oracle and implement lifetime pinning at the narrowest owned seam; prove GREEN and exact-defect mutation RED.
- Sweep CLI, library, MCP, review-bot, and spawned gate-worker entry paths for parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A deterministic synchronized-process reproduction proves the changeable root cause and rules out unrelated import/cache races.
- [ ] A cited contract defines which release/resources remain valid for one invocation.
- [ ] A real parent/child subprocess test is observed RED before repair, GREEN afterward, and RED under exact-defect mutation.
- [ ] A force reinstall during an active gate cannot cause that invocation to raise `ImportError` or `FileNotFoundError` from its resolved release.
- [ ] The next invocation uses the newly installed release; lifetime pinning does not permanently retain obsolete releases.
- [ ] CLI, library, MCP, automated gate callers, and child-process parity are dispositioned.
- [ ] Cleanup behavior and operator setup documentation are updated where the proven mechanism requires it.
compiled_state.title: Concurrent uv tool reinstall can delete the active rebar release during a gate invocation
